verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev documents an official CLI for local dev, self-hosting and deploys, plus a GitHub Actions workflow that deploys tasks on push to main. A programmatic management SDK (runs.list etc.) and scoped, expiring per-environment API keys support headless automation. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of CI/headless use, documentation of non-interactive CI auth and of CI uses beyond deployment (e.g., triggering or testing runs in pipelines).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: This simple GitHub action workflow will deploy your Trigger.dev tasks when new code is pushed to the `main` branch.
The Trigger.dev CLI has a number of options and commands to help you develop locally, self host, and deploy your tasks.
Deploy your Trigger.dev project to the cloud.
Create as many keys as you need per environment, each with its own access scope, optional task restrictions, and an expiration date.
